setup.title: Set up lotse
setup.noToken: This hub is not set up yet. Open the setup link from its log: docker compose logs hub.
setup.invalid: This setup link is not valid. Take the current one from the hub's log; it changes when the hub restarts.
setup.done: This hub is already set up.

database.title: Database
database.description: Where the hub keeps everything. This is fixed once chosen.
database.sqliteHint: One file in the hub's data directory. Nothing to set up; a backup is a copy of the file.
database.postgresHint: A Postgres database you run, for example with the compose file's postgres profile.
database.postgresFound: The compose file's Postgres answers; its address is filled in.

admin.title: Admin
admin.description: The first user, who can do everything. You are logged in right away.
admin.name: Name
admin.urlHint: Where people and agents reach the hub. Agents' install commands use it.

overview.empty: No hosts yet. Start an agent, and its machine appears here.
overview.title: Overview
overview.start: Nothing here yet. Create an environment, then add an agent to it.
overview.noHostsAdd: No hosts yet. Add an agent to a machine, and it shows up here.
overview.addSomething: Add a host or a check
overview.welcomeHint: Start with an environment, such as your shop's production. Then add machines and checks to it.
overview.noHostsYet: No hosts yet. Add one with + Add.
overview.noChecksYet: No checks yet. Add one with + Add.

host.moveHint: Its settings then come from the new environment, and its alerts go where that one's go.
host.waitingHint: {{name}} is named in lotse.yaml, and its settings are ready. Install the agent on the machine with its environment's command (Add host); a machine called {{name}} that enrolls there becomes this host.

update.rolled_back: agent went back from {{version}}, which kept failing to start

chart.empty: No readings in this time range

login.title: Log in to lotse
login.subtitle: Watch over your servers, containers and checks.

tree.newEnvironmentHint: Customer, project and environment. Pick an existing customer or project, or type a new one.
tree.deleteConfirm: Delete this environment? Its history stays.

config.title: Settings
config.description: What applies here, and where it comes from. A value set here wins over those set further up.
config.rulesDescription: When something fires, and how bad it is. Values in bold are set here; the others are inherited, and say from where on hover. Click one to change it here.

agent.addHint: Run this on the machine. The agent connects to the hub, and the machine and its containers appear here within seconds.
agent.systemdHint: Installs lotse to /usr/local/bin and starts it as the service lotse-agent, as user lotse in group docker. Checks the download's checksum.
agent.dockerHint: Runs the agent as a container. It reads the machine through / mounted read-only, and Docker through its socket.
agent.composeHint: The same as a compose file, for a machine managed with docker compose.
agent.localHint: For trying lotse with this repository's compose.yml: starts its agent, on this machine.
agent.tokenHint: The token is this environment's. It is needed once per machine; after that each agent has its own credential.
agent.replaceConfirm: Make a new token? The current one stops working; agents that already enrolled stay connected.
agent.revokeConfirm: Revoke this host's agent? It is disconnected now and can only come back by enrolling again.
agent.revokeHint: Disconnects the agent and revokes its credential. History and readings stay. Running the install command again, with a current token, brings it back.
agent.waiting: Waiting for the machine to connect…

update.installed: {{version}} installed; the agent restarts into it.
update.hubConfirm: Update the hub to {{version}}? It restarts; the page is back within seconds.
update.hubManual: This hub does not run under the starter, so it cannot update itself; pull the newer image.

check.title: Checks

kindHint.http: Fetches a URL from outside: its status after redirects, optionally a word on the page, how long it takes, and its certificate.
kindHint.tls: Opens a TLS connection, for services that are not HTTPS, such as mail on port 465, and watches the certificate.
kindHint.tcp: Connects to a port, such as a database.
kindHint.heartbeat: A job, such as a backup, calls a URL when it ran. If it does not within the period and the grace, the check goes down.

check.keywordHint: A word that must be on the page.
check.name: Name
check.pingHint: Call this URL when the job has run (GET, POST or HEAD); add /fail when it failed. The URL is the secret: keep it out of logs others read.
check.pingAdminOnly: Only admins see the ping URL.
check.deleteConfirm: Delete this check and its results? Its history stays.
check.created: {{name}} added. Its first run comes in a moment.

probe.title: Probes
probe.description: Where checks run from. The hub has its own; probes in other places check from outside, so that a down machine does not take its checker with it.
probe.revokeConfirm: Revoke this probe? It is disconnected and its checks run elsewhere.
probe.addHint: Run this on a machine in another place. It needs no ports and only reaches out to the hub.
probe.name: Name
probe.tokenHint: The token is the hub's probe token; it is needed once per probe. A check runs on all probes unless its setting check.probes says otherwise.

rules.host.load: The load over 5 minutes, per core, is high.
rules.container.unhealthy: A running container's health check fails.
rules.container.restarting: A container stopped this many times in 10 minutes.
rules.check.down: A check failed this many runs in a row, on most of its probes.
rules.check.cert: A certificate expires in fewer days than this.
rules.check.heartbeat: A heartbeat did not come in time, or said its job failed.

alert.title: Alerts
alert.subject: Where
alert.inMaintenance: During maintenance: recorded, but not sent. It is sent when the window ends, if it still fires.
alert.noNotifications: Nothing was sent: notify.channels names no channel here.

channel.title: Channels
channel.description: Where alerts go. Channels defined here can be used here and below, by their key, in notify.channels.

typeHint.email: Sends alerts by email, through the mail server in the settings, or one of its own.
typeHint.googlechat: Posts alerts to a Google Chat space, through the space's webhook.
typeHint.webhook: Posts alerts as JSON to an address, for anything else: a ticket system, a pager, a script.

channel.deleteConfirm: Delete the channel {{key}}? Alerts that name it go nowhere until another channel has its key.
channel.name: Name
channel.ownServer: Send through a mail server of its own

urlHint.googlechat: In the space: Apps & integrations, Webhooks.
urlHint.webhook: Receives a POST with the alerts as JSON.

channel.signingHint: If set, X-Lotse-Signature carries the HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp and the body, so the receiver can tell the message comes from the hub.

hint.value: The hub keeps it sealed and never shows it again.
hint.env: The hub reads the environment variable when it sends; set it in the compose file.
hint.file: The hub reads the file when it sends, from /run/secrets, as Docker secrets are.

mail.title: Mail server
mail.description: The SMTP server email channels send through, unless one has its own.
mail.none: No mail server yet: email channels cannot send.

tlsHint.starttls: Usual on port 587. The hub refuses to send if the server does not offer it.
tlsHint.tls: TLS from the start, usual on port 465.
tlsHint.none: Unencrypted. Only for a mail server on the same machine or network; a password is then only sent to this machine.

mail.removeConfirm: Remove the mail server? Email channels without one of their own stop sending.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.description: While a window is on, alerts here are recorded but not sent. What still fires when it ends is sent then.
maintenance.scheduleHint: Days and a time, in the hub's time zone: daily 04:00-06:00, sun 02:00-04:00, mon-fri 22:00-23:00, mon,thu 01:00-02:00.

nav.searchHint: Find a page, an environment, a host or a check.

add.title: Add
add.where: Which environment does it belong to?
add.environmentFirst: Hosts and checks belong to an environment, such as a shop's production. Create one first.

bell.title: Alerts for {{name}}
bell.description: What is set here applies to this one only. What is not set here comes from above.

environment.title: Create an environment
environment.hint: Hosts and checks belong to one, such as a shop's production: customer, project, environment.

host.title: Add a host
host.hint: One line on the machine; it appears here within seconds, with its containers.

check.title: Add a check
check.hint: A website, a port, or a heartbeat from a backup job.

notify.title: Decide where alerts go
notify.hint: An email address, a Google Chat space or a webhook, so that you hear about problems.

token.title: API tokens
token.description: For lotse apply and export, from a pipeline or a terminal, and for reading through the API. A token works on everything, or on one customer, project or environment and what is in it.
token.newHint: Give it a name that says where it is used, such as "GitHub Actions".
token.name: Name

kindHint.apply: lotse apply changes what is in its scope; lotse export reads it.
kindHint.read: Reads through the API and lotse export; changes nothing.

token.revokeConfirm: Revoke the token {{name}}? Whatever uses it stops working.
token.madeHint: Copy it now: the hub keeps only a hash and cannot show it again.
token.exportHint: Everything as lotse.yaml, to keep in Git and change with lotse apply. Secrets are never in it.
